speaker: READER
text: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.

speaker: READER
text: Now the earth was formless and void, and darkness was over the surface of the deep. And the Spirit of God was hovering over the surface of the waters.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Every other part of the Bible's story is set inside the world this passage describes.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Before there is a fall, a covenant, a nation or a cross, there is a Creator, a good world, and a human race made in His image.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Israel first heard these words as the opening of the Torah, given through Moses to a people who had spent generations in Egypt.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Their neighbours all told their own stories of how the world began.

speaker: GUIDE
text: In Babylon, the god Marduk defeats the sea goddess Tiamat and splits her body to form sky and earth. Human beings are made to carry the labour of the gods, so that the gods may rest.

speaker: GUIDE
text: In Egypt, the sun was worshipped as a god, and Pharaoh was presented as a son of the sun.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Genesis speaks into that world with deliberate restraint. There is no battle. The deep is simply there, and the Spirit of God is over it.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Moses wanted Israel to know who their God was before they learned anything else about Him. Not one god among many, but the Maker of the sun that Egypt worshipped, the sea that the nations feared, and the land they were about to enter.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Verse two names the problem. The earth was formless and void. In Hebrew, tohu wabohu.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Not a description of evil, but of a world not yet shaped and not yet filled. And the six days answer both words in turn.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Days one to three give shape to the formless: light from darkness, the waters above from the waters below, the sea from the dry land.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Days four to six fill the void: lights for the light, birds and fish for the sky and sea, animals and people for the land.

speaker: GUIDE
text: And the seventh day stands apart, as the goal.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Over the deep, the Spirit of God is hovering, the same word used of an eagle over its young. Attentively near, poised to bring life.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Listen for the refrains. And God said. Let there be. And it was so. God saw that it was good. There was evening, and there was morning. The repetition gives the chapter the cadence of worship, and the variations carry the meaning.

speaker: READER
text: And God said,

speaker: GOD
text: “Let there be light,”

speaker: READER
text: and there was light.

speaker: READER
text: And God saw that the light was good, and He separated the light from the darkness.

speaker: READER
text: God called the light “day,” and the darkness He called “night.” And there was evening, and there was morning, the first day.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Light on the first day, before the sun on the fourth. The point is theological before it is astronomical: light comes from God.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Ten times God speaks in this chapter, and each word does what it says. There is no struggle and no strain.

speaker: READER
text: He spoke, and it came to be; He commanded, and it stood firm,

speaker: READER
text: And God said,

speaker: GOD
text: “Let there be an expanse between the waters, to separate the waters from the waters.”

speaker: READER
text: So God made the expanse and separated the waters beneath it from the waters above. And it was so.

speaker: READER
text: God called the expanse “sky.” And there was evening, and there was morning, the second day.

speaker: GUIDE
text: The expanse is raqia, from a verb meaning to spread or beat out, used of hammering gold into thin sheets. The sky is pictured as something God has stretched out over the world, like a craftsman's work.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Day two is the one day the chapter does not close with God's approval. Day three will hear it twice.

chapter: Day Three: land, sea and green
speaker: READER
text: And God said,

chapter: Day Three: land, sea and green
speaker: GOD
text: “Let the waters under the sky be gathered into one place, so that the dry land may appear.”

chapter: Day Three: land, sea and green
speaker: READER
text: And it was so.

chapter: Day Three: land, sea and green
speaker: READER
text: God called the dry land “earth,” and the gathering of waters He called “seas.” And God saw that it was good.

chapter: Day Three: land, sea and green
speaker: READER
text: Then God said,

chapter: Day Three: land, sea and green
speaker: GOD
text: “Let the earth bring forth vegetation: seed-bearing plants and fruit trees, each bearing fruit with seed according to its kind.”

chapter: Day Three: land, sea and green
speaker: READER
text: And it was so.

chapter: Day Three: land, sea and green
speaker: READER
text: The earth produced vegetation: seed-bearing plants according to their kinds and trees bearing fruit with seed according to their kinds. And God saw that it was good.

chapter: Day Three: land, sea and green
speaker: READER
text: And there was evening, and there was morning, the third day.

chapter: Day Three: land, sea and green
speaker: GUIDE
text: Now the three realms stand ready: the light, the sky and the sea, and the dry land. The formless has been given shape.

chapter: Day Three: land, sea and green
speaker: GUIDE
text: But it is still empty.

speaker: READER
text: And God said,

speaker: GOD
text: “Let there be lights in the expanse of the sky to distinguish between the day and the night, and let them be signs to mark the seasons and days and years.

speaker: GOD
text: And let them serve as lights in the expanse of the sky to shine upon the earth.”

speaker: READER
text: And it was so.

speaker: READER
text: God made two great lights: the greater light to rule the day and the lesser light to rule the night. And He made the stars as well.

speaker: READER
text: God set these lights in the expanse of the sky to shine upon the earth,

speaker: READER
text: to preside over the day and the night, and to separate the light from the darkness. And God saw that it was good.

speaker: READER
text: And there was evening, and there was morning, the fourth day.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Notice what is not said. The sun and moon are not even named. To Egypt the sun was a god. Here they are the greater light and the lesser light, lamps hung in the sky with a job to do, and the stars are mentioned almost in passing.

speaker: GUIDE
text: The word for these lights elsewhere names the light of the tabernacle lampstand, and the seasons they mark is the word for Israel's appointed feasts. They are lamps in God's house that keep His calendar.

speaker: READER
text: And God said,

speaker: GOD
text: “Let the waters teem with living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth in the open expanse of the sky.”

speaker: READER
text: So God created the great sea creatures and every living thing that moves, with which the waters teemed according to their kinds, and every winged bird after its kind. And God saw that it was good.

speaker: READER
text: Then God blessed them and said,

speaker: GOD
text: “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the waters of the seas, and let birds multiply on the earth.”

speaker: READER
text: And there was evening, and there was morning, the fifth day.

speaker: GUIDE
text: The great sea creatures, a word that elsewhere names the monsters of the sea, are simply creatures God made and blessed.

speaker: GUIDE
text: And for the first time, God blesses. The whole account moves from emptiness to fullness, because God gives.

chapter: Day Six: the image of God
speaker: READER
text: And God said,

chapter: Day Six: the image of God
speaker: GOD
text: “Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kinds: livestock, land crawlers, and beasts of the earth according to their kinds.”

chapter: Day Six: the image of God
speaker: READER
text: And it was so.

chapter: Day Six: the image of God
speaker: READER
text: God made the beasts of the earth according to their kinds, the livestock according to their kinds, and everything that crawls upon the earth according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.

chapter: Day Six: the image of God
speaker: GUIDE
text: Then the pattern breaks. God does not simply say, let there be. He deliberates.

chapter: Day Six: the image of God
speaker: READER
text: Then God said,

chapter: Day Six: the image of God
speaker: GOD
text: “Let Us make man in Our image, after Our likeness, to rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air, over the livestock, and over all the earth itself, and every creature that crawls upon it.”

chapter: Day Six: the image of God
speaker: READER
text: So God created man in His own image; in the image of God He created him; male and female He created them.

chapter: Day Six: the image of God
speaker: GUIDE
text: Three lines of poetry, and the word created sounds three times.

chapter: Day Six: the image of God
speaker: GUIDE
text: Image, tselem, is the word used for a carved image, the kind Israel was told to destroy in Canaan. In a world full of idols, God places His own living image on the earth.

chapter: Day Six: the image of God
speaker: GUIDE
text: Remember who first heard this. Slaves who had been treated as tools in Pharaoh's building projects are told that every human being, male and female, is made in the image of God and blessed with a royal calling.

chapter: Day Six: the image of God
speaker: READER
text: God blessed them and said to them,

chapter: Day Six: the image of God
speaker: GOD
text: “Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth and subdue it; rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air and every creature that crawls upon the earth.”

chapter: Day Six: the image of God
speaker: GUIDE
text: Humanity is not made to feed the gods. God feeds humanity.

chapter: Day Six: the image of God
speaker: READER
text: Then God said,

chapter: Day Six: the image of God
speaker: GOD
text: “Behold, I have given you every seed-bearing plant on the face of all the earth, and every tree whose fruit contains seed. They will be yours for food.

chapter: Day Six: the image of God
speaker: GOD
text: And to every beast of the earth and every bird of the air and every creature that crawls upon the earth, everything that has the breath of life in it, I have given every green plant for food.”

chapter: Day Six: the image of God
speaker: READER
text: And it was so.

chapter: Day Six: the image of God
speaker: READER
text: And God looked upon all that He had made, and indeed, it was very good. And there was evening, and there was morning, the sixth day.

chapter: Day Six: the image of God
speaker: GUIDE
text: Seven times God looks and calls it good. The last time, very good. The goodness of the world is not a human judgment, but His.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Then the pattern breaks altogether.

speaker: READER
text: Thus the heavens and the earth were completed in all their vast array.

speaker: READER
text: And by the seventh day God had finished the work He had been doing; so on that day He rested from all His work.

speaker: READER
text: Then God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, because on that day He rested from all the work of creation that He had accomplished.

speaker: GUIDE
text: There is no speech. No it was good. No evening and morning. And the Hebrew names the seventh day three times in two verses.

speaker: GUIDE
text: God does not rest because He is tired. He rests because the work is finished, and good.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Then He blesses a day and sanctifies it, the first thing in the Bible to be made holy. Time itself belongs to Him.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Israel would hear an echo. The tabernacle account ends the same way, with the work completed, inspected and blessed. The world is the house God built for Himself, and the tabernacle is a small copy of it in the middle of the camp.

speaker: GUIDE
text: People ask how long these days were. Christians who hold the full truth of Scripture have answered in different ways: ordinary days, long ages, or a framework that sets out God's work like a working week.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Israel's own week was patterned on this one.

speaker: READER
text: For in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth.

speaker: GUIDE
text: But the passage itself presses a different question. Not how long God took, but who He is, and whose the world is.

chapter: In the beginning was the Word
speaker: GUIDE
text: The New Testament does not treat Christ as a latecomer to this story. It places Him at its beginning.

chapter: In the beginning was the Word
speaker: READER
text: In the beginning was the Word,

chapter: In the beginning was the Word
speaker: READER
text: Through Him all things were made, and without Him nothing was made that has been made,

chapter: In the beginning was the Word
speaker: GUIDE
text: Genesis shows God creating by speaking. John tells us that the Speech itself is a person, and that He became flesh.

chapter: In the beginning was the Word
speaker: READER
text: The Light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it.

chapter: In the beginning was the Word
speaker: GUIDE
text: Paul reaches straight for day one to describe what happens when God brings a person to new birth.

chapter: In the beginning was the Word
speaker: READER
text: Let light shine out of darkness,

chapter: In the beginning was the Word
speaker: GUIDE
text: The first creation climbed toward a seventh day. Jesus lies in the tomb through the Sabbath, and rises on the first day of the week. The new creation begins on the first day of a new week.

chapter: In the beginning was the Word
speaker: GUIDE
text: Humanity was made to be God's image. Christ is the image of the invisible God, the true Man in whom the human calling is finally carried out.

chapter: In the beginning was the Word
speaker: GUIDE
text: And the rest of the seventh day, He offers in person.

chapter: In the beginning was the Word
speaker: READER
text: Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest,

chapter: The first page and the last
speaker: GUIDE
text: This page sets the standard for everything after it. Chapter three is a tragedy because chapter one was very good. Death, violence and exile are wrong because they were not part of the world God made.

chapter: The first page and the last
speaker: GUIDE
text: In the flood, the waters of the deep return over the land, a creation undone.

chapter: The first page and the last
speaker: GUIDE
text: The seventh day has no evening. God's rest is the goal of creation, and the rest of Scripture is a long journey toward entering it.

chapter: The first page and the last
speaker: READER
text: There remains, then, a Sabbath rest for the people of God.

chapter: The first page and the last
speaker: GUIDE
text: And the last pages of the Bible deliberately echo the first. A new heaven and a new earth. A city that has no need of sun or moon, for the glory of God is its light. The sea is no more.

chapter: The first page and the last
speaker: GOD
text: Behold, I make all things new.

chapter: The first page and the last
speaker: GUIDE
text: The story that began with, In the beginning God, ends with God dwelling among His people in a world made new.

speaker: GUIDE
text: On the first day God said, let there be light, before the sun existed, because light comes from Him.

speaker: GUIDE
text: Where do you need to ask God to speak light into a dark place?
